# Ongoing Discord Research (Character Channels → Knowledge Docs)

## Idea

Follow Smash Discord channels (eg Mac Nation's per-character channels), use them as a knowledge source, and get
periodic digests of what's relevant. The user decides what goes into `docs/`, and the AI tracks what it has
already read so it only processes new messages.

Related: `personal/ideas.md` item 10 (Smash docs aggregated from web + Discord), and the knowledge-base design in
`spec/pkgs/ds/ai/knowledge_base.md` (layers, staging, provenance).

## Getting messages

| Option | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Manual capture** | Paste threads into `local/staging/discord/`. No setup, within Discord's ToS. Relies on the user remembering |
| **Bot** (preferred long-term) | A Mac Nation mod adds a read-only bot. `ds research discord` fetches new messages through the official API. Automatic and within ToS |
| **Pins / resource channels** | Highest-signal and slow-changing. Use as the initial "base" |
| ❌ **User-token exporters** (eg DiscordChatExporter logged in as the user) | Self-botting breaks Discord's ToS and risks an account ban. Avoid |

Plan: start from pins and resources, then keep up to date with manual capture until a bot is approved.

## Knowing which messages to look at

- **Cursor per channel:** Discord message IDs are time-ordered, so store the last processed ID.

  ```yaml
  # local/staging/discord/_cursors.yaml
  mac-nation/little-mac-general: {last_message_id: 1289…, last_run: 2026-09-30}
  ```
- **Bot fetch:** only messages after the stored ID.
- **Manual capture:** each staged file's header records `covers: <start>..<end>`, so the AI can say where to
  resume.
- **Backfill:** pins and resources first, then history in monthly chunks, oldest first. The cursor moves forward
  as it goes, so a run can stop and resume.

## Filtering (funnel, so the AI never reads a whole channel)

1. **Cheap filter in code, no LLM:** keep messages with frame/percent numbers, glossary or docs keywords, clip
   links, reactions, pins, long reply threads, or a trusted-author list. Group replies into conversations.
2. **AI triage:** extract candidate claims, check them against docs with `search_docs`, and label each one
   **New** / **Confirms** (`docs:line`) / **Contradicts** (`docs:line`).
3. **Digest for the user to review**, eg `local/staging/discord/digests/2026-09-30_mac-labs.md`:

   ```markdown
   # Digest: mac-labs, 2026-09-01 → 2026-09-30   (47 of 1,203 messages kept)
   - [ ] **New** — dtilt → KO punch true at 60–80% on mids — @labber, 14 🔥, [link] → docs/tech.md
   - [ ] **Contradicts** docs/matchups/steve.md:22 — block ledge trap vs getup jump — [link]
   - [x] ~~rejected~~ — joke about Mac recovery
   ```
4. **Integrate** approved items through the smash-research workflow (staging → page → Sources → glossary →
   evals). Decisions stay in the digest so rejected claims don't come back.

## Next steps (when picked up)

1. Add the digest + cursor formats and a "process discord staging" workflow to
   `.agents/skills/smash-research/SKILL.md`.
2. Build the cheap keyword filter as a `ds` command (Typer + shell wrapper, per repo pattern).
3. Ask a Mac Nation mod about a read-only bot, then add `ds research discord` (official API, message-content
   intent, fetch after cursor).
4. Schedule a weekly digest run (Claude Code scheduled task or cron). Tune the filters from digest feedback.

## Considerations

- `local/staging/` is git-ignored and machine-local, so Discord content (other people's words) stays out of a
  possibly public repo. Cursors and digests are machine-local too.
- A bot needs a token stored securely, eg through keyring like the OpenAI key in `ds.settings`.
